R420.note: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) before the delete, matching the existing OrderPolicy::delete and the sibling actions; nothing else changed.

R421.note: Magic-byte check on the opened stream with extension derived from the detected type, then rewind and copy; the ContentType check's removal is stated and a real PNG/JPEG/GIF still uploads.

R422.note: Secure = true added to the existing CookieOptions; nothing else touched.

R423.note: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) against the existing policy method; identical shape to show()/update().

R424.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode on ticketRef at the Response.Write sink; null input still concatenates to empty as before.

R425.note: Keys now come from a hardcoded issuer JWKS URL so the jku resolver is gone, but the write-up adds ValidAlgorithms = RS256 (rejects issuer tokens signed with any other algorithm) and fetches the key set once in the constructor with no refresh, so an issuer key rotation silently fails legitimate tokens until restart.

R426.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() with the OrderContext passed as root keeps property arithmetic working while T(), constructors, method calls and bean refs are rejected, per the contract.

R427.note: Fixed generic 400 body replaces e.getMessage(); status and success path unchanged.

R428.note: rawComment is HTML-entity encoded in the formatter where it is interpolated into summaryHtml; the escapeAuthorName rename is internal and output for benign input is identical.

R429.note: Replacing proc_open with file() + strpos removes the shell entirely, but the whole access log is now loaded into memory instead of streamed through grep (a large log can hit memory_limit) and the error strings change, neither of which the write-up states while claiming identical functionality.

R430.note: unserialize with allowed_classes => [ShoppingCart::class] keeps the cookie format; disallowed classes become __PHP_Incomplete_Class and fall through the existing instanceof guard.

R431.note: password_verify is the right API, but the original == check only worked against plaintext storage, so every existing user fails to log in until the column is rehashed; the write-up states the hash precondition without naming that migration as a required follow-up.

R432.note: escape-html applied to closingNote at the point of interpolation; encoding subject/status too is stated and renders identically for the stored values.

R433.note: bcrypt.compare against user.passwordHash before done(null, user), with a dummy hash for unknown users and the unknown-user path still returning false; the uniform failure message is a stated hardening.

R434.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context) is the documented check for JSON-bound minimal API endpoints; the write-up states clients must now send the token header and that failure throws.

R435.note: encode_entities($cgi->param('note')) calls param in list context, so a duplicated note parameter makes the second value the unsafe-character set and the first value is output unencoded (reproduced with HTML::Entities in the scratch directory: two values leave <script> intact); assign to a scalar first.

R436.note: GetRelativePath closes the sibling-prefix bypass, but for a different-drive absolute path it returns the path unchanged rather than throwing (reproduced with dotnet in the scratch directory: D:\secrets\x.txt passes the .. check), so userFile=D:\... now reads files the original StartsWith check rejected - a regression the write-up wrongly claims is handled.
